edges.description: Provides the direct pH measurement that defines this node, and the largest pH shift of the two models.
edges.limitations: A null allele removes the protein entirely, so it cannot distinguish loss of proton transport from loss of any other function of the subunit. That is precisely what the knock-in below was made to do, and the two must be read together.

edges.description: Establishes that proton transport is the disease-relevant function: removing only the transport raises pH to 6.25 and reproduces the connective-tissue phenotype.
edges.limitations: The pH shift is smaller than the null's, so the two models are not interchangeable, and a phenotype milder in this line than in the null could reflect either residual pumping or a retained non-pumping function of the protein.

edges.description: Reproduces the migration abnormality and the associated seizures, and links them to reduced O-mannosylation of alpha-dystroglycan.
edges.limitations: Graded PARTIALLY_RECAPITULATES because of a specific discordance rather than a general species caveat. The knock-in shows more abnormal migration than the null despite a smaller pH shift, which the simple pH-dose model does not predict, and the human neuronal phenotype is characterised by imaging and clinical features rather than by the histology this readout measures.

nodes.description:
Cortical neurons migrate abnormally, which is the substrate for the developmental delay, seizures and gyration abnormalities seen clinically.
Graded PROVISIONAL for a reason specific to this node rather than to the entry. The abnormal migration itself is directly observed - but in mice, and the human evidence is imaging and clinical rather than histological. More awkwardly, the mouse data run against the intuitive dose-response: the knock-in with the smaller pH shift showed more abnormal migration than the null, correlating with seizures and with reduced O-mannosylation of alpha-dystroglycan. So the neuronal arm does not simply follow the pH gradient the way the skin arm does, and the entry does not pretend otherwise.

nodes.description: The separation-of-function model, and the more informative of the pair. R755Q abolishes V0a2-mediated proton transport while leaving the subunit in place, so any phenotype it produces is attributable to the pumping activity rather than to the protein's presence.
Constitutive null. Trans-Golgi pH 6.52 against a wild-type 5.80, with reduced growth, dermis thickness and elastic fibre formation.

Loss-of-function variants on both alleles of ATP6V0A2, the gene for the a2 subunit of the V-type H+-ATPase. The protein localises to the Golgi apparatus and is absent from patient dermal fibroblasts, so the lesion is loss of the subunit rather than a mislocalised or non-functional protein sitting in place.

nodes.description:
Golgi glycosyltransferases and glycosidases have narrow pH optima, so raising the luminal pH degrades their output. The result is a defect in both N-linked and mucin-type O-linked glycosylation - the combined pattern that places ARCL2A in the congenital disorders of glycosylation and that is detectable in serum by transferrin and apolipoprotein C-III isoelectric focusing.
Which limb matters more is not settled the way the clinical framing implies. The mouse work concludes that altered O-glycosylation is the more relevant limb for the pathomechanism, and that it produces a secondary dystroglycanopathy through reduced O-mannosylation of alpha-dystroglycan - which is a specific, testable route to the neuronal-migration phenotype rather than a general appeal to hypoglycosylation.

nodes.description:
The single physical abnormality from which the rest of the disease follows. Direct measurement in mouse models puts trans-Golgi pH at 5.80 in wild type, 6.25 in a knock-in that abolishes only V0a2-mediated proton transport, and 6.52 in the null - and phenotype severity tracks that gradient rather than tracking whether the protein is present.
The knock-in is what makes this node an established mechanism rather than an inference. It carries an R755Q missense change that selectively removes proton transport while leaving the protein in place, so the pH shift can be attributed to the pumping activity and not to loss of some structural or membrane-fusion role of the subunit.

nodes.description:
Patient fibroblasts show distended Golgi cisternae, abnormal lysosomes and multivesicular bodies, and a delay in brefeldin-A-induced retrograde fusion of Golgi membranes with the endoplasmic reticulum. The delay is specific: it is absent in cells deficient for GORAB or PYCR1, the proteins behind two other autosomal recessive cutis laxa syndromes, so it is a property of the V-ATPase lesion rather than of cutis laxa generally.
Elevated TGF-beta signalling accompanies it, with raised TGF-beta1 in the fibroblast supernatant.

nodes.description:
Epilepsy is the commonest neurological finding in ATP6V0A2 disease and is one of the features that discriminates it from the other autosomal recessive cutis laxa genes. It is enriched in patients ascertained at a younger age.
Banded VERY_FREQUENT on the GeneReviews statement that nearly all affected individuals have seizures. The earlier band rested on an age-at-ascertainment association with a p value, which is not a frequency; GeneReviews supplies the frequency directly and supersedes it.

nodes.description:
Tropoelastin accumulates in the Golgi and forms abnormal intracellular and extracellular aggregates; pulse-chase confirms impaired secretion and increased intracellular retention, and insoluble-elastin assays show significantly reduced deposition of mature extracellular elastin. Apoptosis of elastogenic cells is increased.
Two negatives from the same experiments are what localise the lesion, and they are worth as much as the positive finding. Fibrillin-1 microfibril assembly is normal, and secreted lysyl oxidase activity is normal. So the defect is in getting tropoelastin out of the cell, not in the microfibrillar scaffold it deposits onto and not in the cross-linking step that matures it.
